> 秋水時至，百川灌河；涇流之大，兩涘渚崖之間，不辯牛馬。

Autumn floods arrive, a hundred channels pour into the river, and the current is so wide that between the two banks you cannot tell an ox from a horse.

The river god looks across, sees how small he is, and says the best line in the chapter: 聞道百，以為莫己若者，我之謂也 — "I have heard a hundred things and thought none surpassed me; that is me."

## 自多 is a disease of scale

多: to have much, to be full of oneself. 自多: to consider oneself ample.

The book insists on this: the illness is not moral. It is a matter of 尺度 — of the size of the frame in which you measured. Nothing was wrong with the river. The river had simply never seen the sea.

This distinction decides how the whole chapter reads. If 自多 is a character flaw, the cure is humility, which is another self-assessment. If it is a scale error, the cure is a larger frame, and humility may not be involved at all.

## 拘於虛: the cause is position, not intelligence

拘於虛 — the well-frog is bound by 虛, read 墟: its dwelling.

Note what the sentence does not say. It does not say the frog is stupid. It says the frog is limited by where it lives.

That is a different claim about people. The limit is located in the address, not in the head.

## 尾閭: in and out at the same time

尾閭 is the fabled outlet where the sea drains.

A hundred rivers feed it and it does not overflow; 尾閭 drains it and it does not empty. Both at once — therefore neither increase nor decrease.

This is the chapter's arithmetic, and it is not an argument about moderation. It is an argument that a system with simultaneous inflow and outflow has no level to measure.

## 礨空 and 稊米

礨空: an ant's burrow, some read a small stone hollow. 稊米: the grain of a small grass, minute.

China among the seas is a grain in a warehouse; a person among the ten thousand things is a hair on a horse's body. The scale is not offered as humiliation. It is offered as calibration.

## 倪 and 垺 and the questions that follow

倪: a beginning, a boundary — 惡至而倪貴賤, "where do you draw the line of noble and base?"

垺: large and full — 精，小之微也；垺，大之殷也. The minute is the extreme of small; the vast is the extremity of large. Both are edges of the same scale, and the chapter then shows the scale turning.

## 反衍 and 謝施

反衍: to cycle and spread out. 謝施: to succeed and shift — 謝 as metabolism, 施 as displacement.

Noble and base have no fixed point; the positions keep trading. Much and little do not reside anywhere.

## 落馬首: the line the chapter draws

落 reads 絡: to halter. 落馬首，穿牛鼻 — haltering a horse's head, piercing an ox's nose: that is human. 四足, the four legs: that is 天.

One sentence, and the whole 天／人 boundary is drawn on a body. Not on a doctrine. On a horse's head and an ox's nose.

## The test

Name something you are currently good at. Then ask the two questions the chapter asks of the river: what is the size of the frame in which you measured it, and is the limit on your knowledge a limit of intelligence or a limit of address? If the second, changing address does more than trying harder.
